description: Reserved-word detection in `detect_id_conflicts` (PROTOCOL_SPEC §2.6 step 2, Algorithm A02 family). A reserved word claims a NAMESPACE, not a token, so step 2 tests the FIRST SEGMENT ONLY and segments after the first are unrestricted even when they equal a reserved word. Narrowed in spec v1.26.0 (#99): the algorithm previously read "for each segment", which no SDK implemented and which would make ordinary IDs such as `executor.schema.validate` illegal. Driver contract: for each case, run the SDK's public `register()` path — NOT `register_internal()`, which skips the reserved check by design — with `new_id`, having first registered every id in `existing_ids` (absent means none). `expected` is null when registration succeeds, otherwise the conflict `type`. Assert the outcome and, on a conflict, the reported type. `reserved_words` is the canonical set below; a driver MUST read it from the fixture rather than from its own SDK, so a divergent local list fails the case instead of silently agreeing with itself.

test_cases.note: §2.6 step 2 — the first segment owns the namespace, so this is the case the rule exists for.
An ID with no dot is entirely its own first segment.

THE DISCRIMINATING CASE. Legal in all three SDKs and illegal under the pre-v1.26.0 text; nothing had ever pinned it either way, which is why the divergence survived. `foo.system.bar` is not in the `system` namespace and impersonates nothing.
`schema` is reserved. A per-segment test makes this ordinary ID illegal for no security gain — one of the three examples §2.6 now names explicitly so the narrowing is not reverted.
`core` is reserved and is among the most common words in module naming.
`acl` is reserved; an api-layer module checking ACL state claims nothing.
Matching is per whole segment, not substring: `systems` is not `system`.

Canonical IDs are lowercase (§2.2); a driver whose reserved check is case-sensitive would let this through. If an SDK rejects this earlier as a validation error rather than a conflict, that is conformant — assert only that registration does not succeed.
Step 1 precedes step 2. The same id that is legal above is a duplicate when already registered, and the reported type must be the duplicate, not the reserved word.
